_doc: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for color, citation, and label mapping across the whole Academic_Drawing project. Every skill/agent references tokens by NAME (ink, cond_a, accent, ...), never by raw hex. To restyle the entire project, edit hex values HERE only. Diagram/structural elements use the muted `structural` set; plotted DATA series use the Okabe-Ito `data_series` set (colorblind-safe for >2 categories).

structural._desc: Muted Nature/Cell-toned diagram + layout colors. At most 5 hues coexist on one slide/panel (paper/bg/text do not count toward the 5).

ink.role: primary lines, outlines, primary structure, headings on light

neutral.role: secondary / de-emphasized structure, gridlines, captions, baseline

cond_a.role: condition A / primary entity / stimulus  (NPG teal)

cond_b.role: condition B / contrast entity / response (NPG navy)

accent.role: THE single finding/innovation highlight (NPG coral) — use sparingly, <=1 emphasized region per panel, always paired with weight/shape

data_series._desc: MUTED Nature/Cell-toned categorical palette for PLOTTED data. The first two entries ARE cond_a and cond_b, so a 2-condition plot matches the diagram exactly (same muted blue/terracotta in the figure and the abstract); entries 3+ add more muted hues for additional unnamed levels. These are TONED-DOWN on purpose — do NOT substitute bright Okabe-Ito here. CVD safety comes from the MANDATORY redundant coding (marker shape + line type + direct label, see structural rules), not from saturated color. Consumed by matplotlib via academic_mpl.py (apply_style sets this as the prop_cycle).

_okabe_ito_optin._desc: Bright Okabe-Ito set, available ONLY if a specific figure has many (>4) unnamed categories that must be maximally CVD-separable AND the operator opts in. Not the default; it breaks the toned-down look.

journal_presets._desc: Real journal figure palettes (from the ggsci R package, derived from actual Nature/Science/Lancet/NEJM/JAMA figures). To restyle the whole project: set `active_preset` and copy that preset's first colors into structural.cond_a/cond_b/accent and into data_series.series. These are the 'scientific palettes' to choose from instead of the generic matplotlib blue/orange.

label_map._desc: Project-wide FIXED mapping of each experimental label/condition/emphasis to a structural token. Fill this in once per project (Director owns it) and reuse identically across abstract -> slides -> manuscript. The keys below are a TEMPLATE — replace with the real conditions before producing deliverables.

citation._desc: Short at-a-glance attribution shown on figures/slides (NOT a full reference list).

typography._desc: One sans-serif family across the whole project. Arial/Helvetica are confirmed present and are the Cell/Nature default.
typography.case: sentence case (not Title Case, not ALL CAPS except acronyms)
typography._minima_note: Hard illegibility floors (pt at final size); venue-spec SoT is ga-templates Step 0. Cell GA recommended 12-16pt, hard floor 9pt.
